Attach survey data to a frame

Source: R/data.R
areal_data.Rd

Assigns each survey to an areal unit and a time step, then pools surveys that fall in the same unit and step: positives add, and so do the numbers tested. The pooled cells are the only data the model sees. Surveys that cannot be used are kept, with the reason, so that every exclusion can be accounted for: print the result to see them.

Usage

areal_data(
  data,
  frame,
  time,
  y,
  k,
  area = NULL,
  coords = NULL,
  crs = 4326,
  date = NULL,
  t = NULL,
  snap_max_m = 10000,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

A data frame, one row per survey.

frame

A areal_frame().

time

A time_frame().

y, k

Names of the columns holding the number of positives and the number tested.

area

Name of a column of unit ids matching frame$ids. Give this or coords.

coords

Names of the x and y (longitude and latitude) columns. Needs a frame built from polygons.

crs

Coordinate reference system of coords (default WGS84 longitude/latitude).

date

Name of a column of dates (Date, date-times, or "YYYY-MM-DD" text). Give this or t.

t

Name of a column of time steps: step numbers (1..n_steps), or the time frame's labels (e.g. "2020-03"). Required for a plain index time frame.

snap_max_m

Maximum distance (metres) for snapping points outside every polygon to the nearest unit. Use 0 for no snapping.

verbose

Report, in one line, how many surveys were used and how many cells they make.

Value

An object of class stareal_data:

cells

one row per observed cell, ordered by cell_id ((area - 1) * n_steps + t): cell_id, area (row of the frame), id, t, time (label), y, k, n_surveys

surveys

data with .id (the area id, NA if none), .t, .snap_m and .excluded (NA if used, otherwise the reason) added

frame, time

the frame and time frame

truth

NULL (see simulate_areal())

Print it for the exclusions; plot() shows where and when the data are.

Details

Reasons for exclusion, checked in this order:

  • missing or invalid counts: y or k missing or unreadable, not whole numbers, negative, k = 0, or y > k. These come with a warning, because they are usually data errors.

  • missing area, or missing or unreadable coordinates;

  • area id not in the frame. This also comes with a warning.

  • outside the frame: coordinates more than snap_max_m from every unit;

  • missing date or time step;

  • unreadable date (not YYYY-MM-DD), or a time step that is not a step number or label of the time frame. These come with a warning.

  • outside the time window.

Points that fall outside every polygon but within snap_max_m of one are assigned to the nearest unit. Survey coordinates are often rounded, and coastal sites fall just offshore. Snap distances are recorded in $surveys$.snap_m. A point inside two overlapping units goes to the first, with a warning.

Examples

fr <- areal_lattice(3, 3)
tf <- time_frame(n_steps = 4)
surveys <- data.frame(unit = c("r1c1", "r1c1", "r2c3", "r9c9"),
                      step = c(1, 1, 4, 2), pos = c(3, 1, 0, 2), n = c(10, 5, 8, 9))
d <- areal_data(surveys, fr, tf, y = "pos", k = "n", area = "unit", t = "step")
#> Warning: 1 survey with area ids not in the frame
#> 3 of 4 surveys used, pooled into 2 cells (print the result for the exclusions)
d
#> <stareal_data> 3 of 4 surveys used, pooled into 2 cells
#>   2 of 9 units and 2 of 4 time steps have data (5.56% of the 36 area-time cells)
#>   tested per cell: median 11.5, range 8-15; total 23 tested, 4 positive
#>   excluded:
#>          1  area not in frame
d$cells
#>    cell_id area   id t time y  k n_surveys
#> 1        1    1 r1c1 1    1 4 15         2
#> 24      24    6 r2c3 4    4 0  8         1
